title: [B2 • Band 6.0] Bài 212: Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 212 (LEVEL B2 • BAND 6.0)

Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B

Paragraph A. In the spring of 1900, British archaeologist Sir Arthur Evans began excavating at Knossos on Crete. Within days, his team uncovered the sprawling Bronze Age palace he linked to the mythical King Minos. Alongside painted wall frescoes and giant storage jars lay thousands of hardened clay tablets bearing two unfamiliar scripts. Evans named the older pictographic script Linear A and the younger, more angular script Linear B. Convinced he had discovered a unique non-Greek civilisation, Evans tightly restricted access to the tablets and insisted their language had zero connection to classical Greek.

Paragraph B. For over four decades, Linear B resisted every attempt at translation. Because the clay tablets were originally intended as temporary administrative notes, they survived into modern times only because catastrophic palace fires baked the soft clay into durable ceramic. Progress was further blocked by the lack of a bilingual text like the Rosetta Stone—which paired Egyptian hieroglyphs with readable Greek—leaving Evans to pass away in 1941 without reading a single word.

Paragraph C. The crucial breakthrough came not from a famous professor, but from an uncelebrated American classicist named Alice Kober. Working steadily at Brooklyn College during the 1940s, Kober cut thousands of index cards from old exam papers because of wartime paper shortages. She observed that groups of signs shared identical opening symbols while ending differently, functioning like grammatical case endings in Latin. Before dying in 1950, Kober constructed a rigorous mathematical grid charting recurring consonants and vowels, proving Linear B was a phonetic syllabary.

Paragraph D. Kober's grid passed to Michael Ventris, a brilliant British architect fascinated by ancient codes. Although Ventris initially assumed Linear B recorded an Etruscan dialect, plugging known phonetic values into Cretan place-names—such as A-mi-ni-so (Amnisos) and Ko-no-so (Knossos)—produced unmistakably Greek sounds. On 1 July 1952, Ventris announced on BBC radio that Linear B was archaic Greek written five centuries before Homer.

Paragraph E. Collaborating with Cambridge philologist John Chadwick, Ventris confirmed that Linear B represented Mycenaean Greek, the administrative language of mainland warrior rulers who controlled the Aegean during the late Bronze Age. Rather than heroic poetry or state treaties, the tablets proved to be thorough accounting ledgers listing barley, olive oil, sheep, bronze arrowheads, and palace workers.

Paragraph F. Equally significant, the deciphered inventories recorded religious offerings to deities well known from later classical Athens, including Greek gods such as Zeus, Poseidon, and Athena. By proving an unbroken cultural bridge between Bronze Age Mycenae and classical Greece, solving Linear B pushed the verified history of the Greek language back by more than five hundred years.

groups.title: Questions 9–12
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: how testing local geographical names led to a major radio announcement

steps: Đoạn D: Thử giá trị âm vào địa danh Amnisos, Knossos rồi công bố trên đài BBC.

q2.text: the accidental reason fragile administrative notes survived for millennia

steps: Đoạn B: Cháy cung điện vô tình nung đất sét mềm thành gốm cứng.

q3.text: religious evidence proving an unbroken cultural link to classical Athens

steps: Đoạn F: Lễ vật dâng thần Zeus, Poseidon, Athena chứng minh mạch văn hóa liền mạch.

q4.text: how a researcher worked using improvised materials during wartime

steps: Đoạn C: Alice Kober cắt thẻ từ giấy thi cũ vì thiếu giấy thời chiến.
Đoạn B: "...catastrophic palace fires baked the soft clay..."
Đoạn F: "...including Greek gods such as Zeus..."

q9.text: Sir Arthur Evans rejected the possibility that Linear B could be related to Greek.

steps: Đoạn A: Evans khẳng định ngôn ngữ này không hề liên quan tới tiếng Hy Lạp cổ.

q10.text: Alice Kober published the complete translation of the Knossos tablets in 1950.

steps: Đoạn C & D: Kober qua đời năm 1950 sau khi lập bảng lưới toán học; phải tới năm 1952 Ventris mới giải mã được.

q11.text: Michael Ventris studied ancient languages at Oxford University before becoming an architect.

steps: Đoạn D: Bài chỉ nói Ventris là kiến trúc sư người Anh đam mê mật mã cổ, không nhắc Đại học Oxford.

q12.text: The deciphered tablets contained practical economic records rather than literature.

steps: Đoạn E: Không phải sử thi mà là sổ kế toán ghi chép lúa mạch, dầu ô-liu, cừu, vũ khí.
